title_en: Dalian Yuandong Housing Development Co., Ltd. v. Liaoning Jinli Housing Industry Company and Liaoning Aojinli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights
ruling_gist_en: First, according to Articles 79 and 80 of the Contract Law of the PRC, a creditor may transfer all or part of its contractual rights to a third party, and such transfer only requires notification to the debtor without needing the debtor's consent. Therefore, once the transfer is completed, the original creditor is no longer the subject of the contractual rights, i.e., it loses the qualification to claim contractual rights against the debtor in its own name as a creditor.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over contract for transfer of state-owned land use rights; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Liaoning Province; Legal person; Contract Law; Effect of assignment of creditor's rights; Determination of repetitive lawsuit; Dismissal of claims; Transfer of land use rights; Assignment of creditor's rights; Repetitive lawsuit; Contract dispute; Land use rights; Dispute over contract for transfer of land use rights
full_text_en:
Dalian Yuandong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Liaoning Jinli Real Estate Company and Liaoning Aojinli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Dispute over State-owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract

Ruling Summary

1. Pursuant to Articles 79 and 80 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a creditor may assign all or part of its contractual rights to a third party, and such assignment requires only notification to the debtor, not the debtor's consent. Therefore, once the assignment is completed, the original creditor is no longer the subject of the contractual rights and thus loses the qualification to claim contractual rights against the debtor in its own name.

2. If a party's lawsuit is dismissed by a people's court through a ruling that has become legally effective, and the party disagrees with that ruling, it may not assert content contrary to the effective ruling in subsequent litigation, nor may it institute another action on the same subject matter, except by lawfully initiating a retrial procedure to retry the case.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

No. 95 (2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Dalian Yuandong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 2 Minquan North Second Street, Shahekou District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Liu Bingqiang, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.

Agents ad litem: Yu Yun, Deputy General Manager of Dalian Daxian Group Co., Ltd., Liaoning Province.

Xu Zhenguo, lawyer of Hainan Jinyu Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance): Liaoning Jinli Real Estate Company, domiciled at No. 58 Shisanwei Road, Shenhe District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Bai Baoshan, Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Ge Changsheng, lawyer of Liaoning Shengjing Law Firm.

Zhang Jianhua, lawyer of Liaoning People's Law Firm.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance): Liaoning Aojinli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 58 Shisanwei Road, Shenhe District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Wan Jiting, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.

Agent ad litem: Hua Zegeng, staff member of the company.

Zhang Jianhua, lawyer of Liaoning People's Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a state-owned land use rights transfer contract between the appellant, Dalian Yuandong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuandong Company), and the appellees, Liaoning Jinli Real Estate Company (hereinafter referred to as Jinli Company) and Liaoning Aojinli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aojinli Company), the Liaoning High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (No. 9 (2004) Liao Min Yi Fang Chu Zi) on August 15, 2005. Yuandong Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on November 29, 2005. The following persons appeared in court to participate in the proceedings: Xu Zhenguo and Yu Yun, agents ad litem of the appellant Yuandong Company; Bai Baoshan, legal representative of the appellee Jinli Company, and Ge Changsheng, its agent ad litem; Hua Zegeng, agent ad litem of the appellee Aojinli Company; and Zhang Jianhua, agent ad litem of both Jinli Company and Aojinli Company. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial: On December 20, 1991, Yuandong Company and the non-party China International Yacht Club (hereinafter referred to as the Yacht Club) entered into the "Joint Development of Jinshitan Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Development Contract"), stipulating that the Yacht Club would transfer to Yuandong Company the land use rights of 100,000 square meters of land within its development zone at a price of RMB 80 per square meter, with a transfer term of 49 years and a total transfer price of RMB 8 million. The contract only stated that the land parcel was in Groups 1, 2, and 3 on the south seaside of the public building area, without indicating the boundaries of the transferred area, and provided that the specific location would be subject to the planning plan. On October 8, 1992, the Yacht Club and the Dalian Land Administration Bureau signed the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract," stipulating that the Dalian Land Administration Bureau would grant to the Yacht Club the land use rights of 460,000 square meters of land located within the Jinshitan National Tourist Resort, with a grant term of 49 years and a grant fee of RMB 20 per square meter. This "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" did not indicate the boundaries of the granted land, only stating that details were set forth in the attached geographic location map of the land parcel. However, the location of the green line area circled in the geographic location map was not in the same place as the land parcel transferred by the Yacht Club to Yuandong Company. On January 29, 1993, Yuandong Company and Jinli Company signed the "Joint Development of Land for Consideration Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Joint Development Agreement"), stipulating that Yuandong Company would transfer to Jinli Company the land use rights of 86,000 square meters of land in the member villa area of the Jinshitan Yacht Club, for which Yuandong Company had already acquired the use rights, at a price of RMB 320 per square meter, with a use term of 48 years and a total transfer price of RMB 27.52 million (the transferred land area was subject to the area within the final surveyed planning red line as confirmed by both parties). Yuandong Company was to provide Jinli Company with the land use certificate for the transferred land parcel, the attached map, and the revised and finalized detailed planning plan and planning requirements. Within five days after the signing of the agreement, Jinli Company was required to pay a deposit of RMB 2 million to Yuandong Company, no less than RMB 18 million by the end of March 1993, and the full balance of the transfer fee by the end of April of the same year. If Jinli Company failed to pay the amounts due on time, in addition to bearing Yuandong Company's economic losses, Yuandong Company could recover the land use rights for the unpaid portion. The supporting fees within the red line of the transferred land parcel were to be borne by Jinli Company; the supporting fees outside the red line were to be paid by Jinli Company to Yuandong Company in advance in accordance with the Yacht Club's requirements, and Yuandong Company would pay them uniformly to the Yacht Club.

On January 31, 1993, Yuandong Company issued a self-printed "Land Use Certificate" to Jinli Company, which stated that Jinli Company was jointly developing the member villa area project of the Yacht Club within the planned land area of the Jinshitan Yacht Club, using a land area of 86,000 square meters, with a use term of 49 years.

To perform the above agreement, Jinli Company paid a deposit of RMB 2 million to Yuandong Company and subsequently paid transfer fees of RMB 11.5 million, totaling RMB 13.5 million. Among these payments, the RMB 10 million paid on April 30, 1993, was borrowed by Jinli Company from the non-party China Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Company, Liaoning Branch (hereinafter referred to as Metals Company), and was remitted directly by Metals Company to Yuandong Company. Yuandong Company issued a receipt for this payment to Jinli Company on July 31, 1994.

On February 27, 1995, Yuandong Company issued a written "Notice on Urging Payment of Land Supporting Fees" to Aojinli Company. The notice, addressed to Aojinli Company (formerly Liaoning Jinli Company), stated in substance: "You have paid land fees of RMB 13.5 million, equivalent to 42,187.5 square meters of land. The supporting fees outside the land area are RMB 220 per square meter, totaling RMB 9,281,250. As required by the Yacht Club, the supporting fees must be paid in full by the end of March 1995. If you wish to retain the land of 42,187.5 square meters, you must pay the supporting fees in full on time; otherwise, the land cannot be retained. If the paid amount of RMB 13.5 million is used to pay land fees and supporting fees (RMB 540 per square meter), you would receive 25,000 square meters of land. If you choose the first option, please pay all supporting fees on time; otherwise, in accordance with the second option, 25,000 square meters of land will be allocated to you, and the land certificate for 25,000 square meters will be processed for you."

On March 5, 1995, Aojinli Company sent a reply to Yuandong Company (neither party could provide Aojinli Company's reply). On March 10, 1995, Yuandong Company sent a further reply to Aojinli Company, stating: "Your reply dated March 5, 1995, has been received. In view of the current situation and the opinions in your reply, we propose two options for your choice and request that you inform us of your decision: (1) The paid amount of RMB 13.5 million should be allocated to 25,000 square meters of land. Due to planning adjustments, the location has slightly changed. There is a land parcel of 27,800 square meters that can be entirely allocated to you, and the land certificate will be processed for your company. The economic issues concerning the additional 2,800 square meters will be discussed later. In this case, your company can operate independently or jointly with us. (2) Alternatively, the land can be handed over to our company for unified operation. After operation, the principal of RMB 13.5 million will be returned to your company. If the operation yields profits, partial or full interest will be considered for payment to your company. If the operation is unsuccessful, only the principal will be repaid without interest." On November 17, 1995, Yuandong Company issued a letter to Aojinli Company stating: "Yuandong Company borrowed RMB 13.5 million from Aojinli Company in installments beginning in 1992 and is currently unable to repay. Upon negotiation between the parties, it is agreed that this loan will be repaid in four installments in 1996: RMB 4 million in January, RMB 5 million in March, RMB 3 million in June, and RMB 1.5 million in September." On November 18, 1995, Bai Baoshan (then the finance director of Metals Company and assisting in managing Aojinli Company's financial work) issued a written "Statement on Fund Utilization" to Yuandong Company, stating: "This document is for the interests of both parties and for internal use. I, as the handling party, hereby state this." Bai Baoshan, during the hearing of the case of Aojinli Company v. Yuandong Company on land use rights transfer dispute (No. 310 (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi) concluded by the court of first instance on March 12, 2004, acknowledged the authenticity of this statement in court and pointed out that "this document" referred to the letter dated November 17, 1995, in which Yuandong Company agreed to repay Aojinli Company in installments. On August 30, 1996, Yuandong Company issued a letter titled "Agreement" to Aojinli Company, stating: "Yuandong Company began receiving funds of RMB 13.5 million from Aojinli Company in installments in 1992. If economic conditions improve, the repayment will be completed by July 1999 in three installments. If economic conditions do not improve, the repayment plan will be deferred on an annual basis."

On April 22, 1997, the Yacht Club submitted to the Dalian Jinshitan National Tourist Resort Management Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Resort Management Committee) a "Report on Land Adjustment," stating: "The 1,141,197 square meters of construction planning land approved for the Yacht Club has been occupied by the Resort Management Committee by 338,361 square meters. The occupied land involves three other cooperative development entities that have already paid the price. These cooperative development entities have repeatedly requested the allocation of land for construction. We request the Resort Management Committee to return the occupied land to facilitate coordination with the cooperative development entities. If return is not possible, we suggest adjusting the land at the edge of our area to us to maintain the integrity of our project." On September 24, 1997, Yuandong Company and the Yacht Club signed the "Contract for Cooperative Development of Dalian Jinshitan Land," indicating that this contract was one of the transfer contracts within the 460,000 square meters of transferable land determined by Article 5 of the "State-owned Land Grant Contract" signed between the Yacht Club and the Dalian Land Bureau in October 1992. It was stipulated that the Yacht Club would transfer to Yuandong Company 70,000 square meters of land within its total planned area of 1 million square meters, with a transfer term of 49 years, a land transfer fee of RMB 80 per square meter, supporting fees of RMB 220 per square meter, totaling RMB 300 per square meter, and a total transfer price of RMB 21 million.

On March 24, 1999, the Yacht Club and the Resort Management Committee signed the "Agreement on Exchange of Construction Land," stipulating that the total area of construction land occupied by the Resort Management Committee and to be supplied to the Yacht Club was 317,844 square meters, and the Resort Management Committee would exchange 235,217.74 square meters of adjacent land with the Yacht Club's construction land. Because the Resort Management Committee adjusted the Yacht Club's construction land, Yuandong Company was unable to deliver the seaside land parcel to Jinli Company as agreed.

In July 1999, Yuandong Company obtained "State-owned Land Use Certificates" No. 00006 (1999) and No. 00007 (1999) issued by Dalian Jinshitan National Tourist Resort, with a total land use right area of 70,000 square meters (the land under these two certificates was not the land parcel agreed upon between Yuandong Company and Jinli Company in the agreement).

On July 2, 1999, the non-party Metals Company filed a lawsuit with the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province against Aojinli Company and Yuandong Company, alleging that Aojinli Company had borrowed RMB 10 million from Metals Company and paid it to Yuandong Company but had not repaid it, and requesting that Aojinli Company and Yuandong Company be ordered to repay the principal and interest promptly. Aojinli Company admitted to borrowing the funds from Metals Company. Yuandong Company argued that there was no legal relationship between Yuandong Company and Metals Company and that it should not bear the repayment obligation. The Shenyang Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment (No. 440 (1999) Shen Jing Chu Zi) holding that there was no loan legal relationship between Metals Company and Yuandong Company, and ordering Aojinli Company to repay the principal. The judgment has become legally effective.

Previously, in 2000, Aojinli Company had filed a lawsuit against Yuandong Company with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on a dispute over joint land development. On April 4, 2000, Aojinli Company applied to withdraw the lawsuit on the ground of incorrect parties. On April 10, 2000, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil ruling (No. 29 (2000) Da Min Fang Chu Zi) granting the withdrawal.

On March 12, 2002, Aojinli Company served on Yuandong Company, through notarized delivery, a "Notice of Urging Payment of Debt" jointly stamped by Jinli Company and Aojinli Company. The notice stated that the creditor was Aojinli Company and formally notified Dalian Daxian Group Co., Ltd. and Yuandong Company that the RMB 13.5 million paid as land use rights transfer fees to Yuandong Company had all been provided by Aojinli Company. This notice could serve as a transfer of rights, and Aojinli Company requested Yuandong Company to repay the principal and interest as soon as possible.

On September 23, 2002, Aojinli Company again filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court, requesting confirmation that the "Joint Development Agreement" between Yuandong Company and Jinli Company was invalid and that Yuandong Company should return the investment of RMB 13.5 million and pay interest for the period of possession of the funds. On October 16, 2003, the Dalian Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment (No. 109 (2002) Da Min Fang Chu Zi), holding that although Yuandong Company had not obtained the land use rights at the time of signing the contract, it had obtained them before the lawsuit was filed, so the contract was valid; that the three repayment agreements of Yuandong Company were not its true expressions of intent; and that Aojinli Company's claims should be dismissed. Both Aojinli Company and Yuandong Company appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court. Aojinli Company's ground for appeal was that the first-instance judgment erred in finding that the three repayment agreements were not true expressions of intent, and requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment and support for its claims. Yuandong Company's ground for appeal was that the first-instance judgment erred in the application of law and that Aojinli Company's lawsuit should be dismissed by ruling. On March 12, 2004, the Liaoning High People's Court rendered a civil ruling (No. 310 (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi), holding that no legal relationship of simultaneous assignment of contractual rights and obligations had been formed among Yuandong Company, Jinli Company, and Aojinli Company; that the subject of the "Joint Development Agreement" was Jinli Company; and that a party outside the contract had no right to request a declaration of invalidity of a contract between others, thus ruling to dismiss Aojinli Company's lawsuit.

The court of first instance further found: Aojinli Company was a joint venture established by Jinli Company, Metals Company, and Australia China Resources Co., Ltd. On September 14, 1992, Shenyang Branch of China Nonferrous Metals Industry Corporation, the parent company of Metals Company, issued Document No. 348 (1992) Zhong Se Shen Ban Zi, deciding to establish a Sino-foreign equity joint venture, Aojinli Company. On December 14, 1992, the Liaoning Provincial Commission of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, by Document No. 654 (1992) Liao Wai Jing Mao Zi Zi, approved the establishment of Aojinli Company as a joint venture by Jinli Company, Metals Company, Liaoning Yida International Investment Service Company (hereinafter referred to as Yida Company), and Australia Asia Pacific Resources Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Asia Pacific Company), with a registered capital of RMB 10 million. Of this total investment of RMB 10 million, Jinli Company invested RMB 3.5 million, Metals Company invested RMB 3 million, Yida Company invested RMB 1 million, and Asia Pacific Company contributed the equivalent of RMB 2.5 million in U.S. dollar cash. Aojinli Company was approved and registered by the Liaoning Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce on June 17, 1993.

On April 6, 2004, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that Jinli Company was a major shareholder of Aojinli Company; that Jinli Company, acting as agent for Aojinli Company, signed the "Joint Development Agreement" with Yuandong Company on January 29, 1993; that Jinli Company subsequently remitted land transfer fees totaling RMB 13.5 million to Yuandong Company in installments; that Yuandong Company self-prepared a "Land Use Certificate" and issued four unregulated receipts to Aojinli Company; that Aojinli Company recorded the RMB 13.5 million investment as part of its construction-in-progress investment cost line item and attached the four unregulated receipts to the corresponding investment item; that because Yuandong Company failed to obtain the land use rights for the land parcel as agreed in the contract, Yuandong Company had three times in writing promised to repay the RMB 13.5 million investment to Aojinli Company but had not actually repaid; that Yuandong Company's long-term possession of the funds caused Jinli Company and Aojinli Company interest and other losses totaling RMB 17 million; that Yuandong Company should bear the fault liability for the improper transaction; and that Yuandong Company should be ordered to return the investment principal and interest totaling RMB 30.5 million and bear all litigation costs.

During the first-instance proceedings, at the second hearing of the court of first instance, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company added a claim requesting a declaration that the "Joint Development Agreement" signed on January 29, 1993, was invalid.

Yuandong Company argued in its defense: Jinli Company claimed in its complaint that it was the agent of Aojinli Company; Yuandong Company argued that an agent had no right to assert substantive rights and lacked standing as a party, so Jinli Company's lawsuit should be dismissed. Aojinli Company claimed in its complaint that it was the subject of the contract and the actual investor and payer; however, the Liaoning High People's Court, by civil ruling No. 310 (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi, held that Aojinli Company had no right to claim against Yuandong Company and dismissed Aojinli Company's lawsuit; therefore, Aojinli Company's lawsuit in this case should also be dismissed.

After the hearing of the court of first instance, Yuandong Company supplemented its defense, arguing: Jinli Company's claim as the substantive right holder was time-barred; the contract signed by the parties was legal and valid; and Jinli Company should be required to continue performing the contract or bear liability for breach of contract.

The court of first instance held that the nature of the "Joint Development Agreement" signed by both parties was a contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights. Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Real Estate Development and Operation Before the Implementation of the Law on the Administration of Real Estate" provides: "The transferor in a transfer contract shall be the land user who has legally completed the procedures for land use right registration or alteration registration and obtained the land use certificate. Contracts signed by a land user who has not obtained the land use certificate as the transferor with others shall generally be deemed invalid, except that the transferor has invested in and developed the land in accordance with the period and conditions stipulated in the transfer contract and, during the first-instance trial, has obtained approval from the relevant competent authority and retroactively completed the procedures for land use right registration or alteration registration, in which case the contract may be deemed valid." Because Far East Company failed to obtain the land use right for the 86,000-square-meter member villa area of the Jinshitan Yacht Club when signing the "Joint Development Agreement" with Jinli Company, and the land under the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" obtained by Far East Company on July 19, 1997, was not the location of the agreed-upon transferred plot, Far East Company did not obtain the land use right for the plot agreed to be transferred under the agreement between the parties. Therefore, the "Joint Development Agreement" signed by the parties should be deemed invalid. Far East Company, as the transferor under the state-owned land transfer contract, should bear the primary responsibility for the invalidity of the contract. Jinli Company, by signing the contract without knowing whether Far East Company had obtained the land use right, should also bear certain responsibility for the invalidity of the contract. Jinli Company's claim that the contract was invalid and its request for Far East Company to return the already paid land transfer fee of RMB 13.5 million should be supported. However, Jinli Company's claim for Far East Company to pay all the interest cannot be supported. Because Jinli Company failed to properly exercise its right to sue, causing a delay of up to 12 years in the litigation, which increased the interest loss, Jinli Company should bear primary responsibility for the increased interest loss. However, during the performance of the agreement, Far East Company had issued repayment plans to Aojinli Company on multiple occasions, which was also one of the reasons why Aojinli Company filed the lawsuit in its own name. Therefore, Far East Company should also bear certain responsibility for Jinli Company and Aojinli Company's failure to properly exercise their right to sue. Considering the fault and responsibility of both parties comprehensively, Far East Company bears the primary responsibility, bearing 60% of the interest loss, and Jinli Company bears the secondary responsibility, bearing 40% of the interest loss.

Regarding Jinli Company's claim that it signed the "Joint Development Agreement" as an agent of Aojinli Company. The agreement was signed by Jinli Company and Far East Company on January 29, 1993. Although the Liaoning Provincial Economic and Trade Commission approved in a reply on December 14, 1992, the establishment of Aojinli Company as a joint venture by Jinli Company, Jinshu Company, Yida Company, and Yatai Company, the date of Aojinli Company's registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce was June 17, 1993. Aojinli Company's legal personality should commence from the date of its registration. When Jinli Company signed the agreement with Far East Company, Aojinli Company did not have the legal personality of a legal person. Jinli Company could not sign the agreement on behalf of Aojinli Company, which had no legal personality. Therefore, Jinli Company's claim that it signed the agreement as an agent of Aojinli Company is not supported.

Regarding the question of whether Aojinli Company has the right to assert claims against Far East Company. Aojinli Company is not a party to the contract. Aojinli Company's assertion of claims against Far East Company in another case was already dismissed by the court in a ruling. Therefore, Aojinli Company's re-filing of a lawsuit before the court on the same cause of action is not supported.

Regarding the question of whether Jinli Company has asserted its own rights. Jinli Company and Aojinli Company filed the lawsuit as co-plaintiffs. Jinli Company stated in its court statements and written agency submissions that it was asserting rights jointly with Aojinli Company. Although in the complaint, Jinli Company claimed it was signing the contract as an agent of Aojinli Company, it never stated that it had waived its own rights. When informed that the claim that Jinli Company signed the contract as an agent for Aojinli Company with Far East Company was not established, Jinli Company stated that if the court determined that the contract was signed by Jinli Company and Far East Company, Jinli Company would explicitly assert its own rights. Therefore, it should be determined that Jinli Company has asserted its own rights in this case. Far East Company's contention that Jinli Company did not actually assert its own rights is not established and is not supported.

Regarding the question of whether Jinli Company's claim exceeded the statute of limitations. After Far East Company issued a receipt to Jinli Company on July 31, 1994, from February 27, 1995, to August 30, 1996, it sent four written notices to Aojinli Company, negotiating or promising to repay RMB 13.5 million. The first notice was addressed to Aojinli Company (formerly Jinli Company). The last repayment commitment letter promised repayment by July 1999 and stated that if the economic situation did not improve, the repayment plan would be deferred on an annual basis. In April 2000, Aojinli Company filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province and later withdrew the lawsuit. On March 12, 2002, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company jointly issued a "Notice of Demand for Payment of Arrears" to Far East Company. On September 23, 2002, Aojinli Company again filed a lawsuit, and the Liaoning Provincial High People's Court rendered a final ruling on March 12, 2004. On April 6, 2004, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company jointly filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance against Far East Company as the defendant. Based on the above facts, Jinli Company's assertion of its rights in this case did not exceed the statute of limitations.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 58 and 61 of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Real Estate Development and Operation Before the Implementation of the Law on the Administration of Real Estate," the judgment is as follows: (1) The "Joint Development Agreement" signed by Far East Company and Jinli Company on January 29, 1993, is invalid; (2) Far East Company shall, within 15 days after the judgment takes effect, return to Jinli Company the land transfer fee of RMB 13.5 million, and pay to Jinli Company 60% of the interest on this amount at the loan interest rate of the China Construction Bank for the corresponding period (the starting time for interest payment: for RMB 2 million, from January 31, 1993, until the date of payment; for RMB 10 million, from April 30, 1993, until the date of payment; for RMB 1 million, from October 30, 1993, until the date of payment; for RMB 500,000, from January 11, 1994, until the date of payment); (3) Dismiss Jinli Company's other claims; (4) Dismiss Aojinli Company's claims. Court acceptance fee of RMB 162,510 and preservation fee of RMB 68,020, totaling RMB 230,530, to be borne by Far East Company in the amount of RMB 180,000, by Jinli Company in the amount of RMB 50,530, and other travel expenses of RMB 5,000 to be borne by Far East Company.

Far East Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court on the grounds that the first-instance court committed procedural violations, made factual errors, and improperly applied the law. It requested: 1. Reversal of the first-instance judgment; 2. Dismissal of Jinli Company's claims; 3. Litigation costs to be borne by Jinli Company and Aojinli Company. The main reasons are as follows: (1) Procedural violations by the first-instance court. First, the first-instance court's acceptance of this case violated the fundamental civil litigation principle of res judicata (no second action on the same matter). On September 23, 2002, Aojinli Company filed a lawsuit against Far East Company as the defendant with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province, seeking a determination that the "Joint Development Agreement" was invalid and an order for Far East Company to return the investment of RMB 13.5 million and interest of RMB 6 million for the period of its occupation of the funds. The Dalian Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2002) Da Min Fang Chu Zi No. 109, dismissing Aojinli Company's claims. Aojinli Company, dissatisfied with this judgment, appealed to the Liaoning Provincial High People's Court. The Liaoning Provincial High People's Court dismissed Aojinli Company's lawsuit by Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310, which has become legally effective. If Aojinli Company was dissatisfied with this effective ruling, it should have pursued a retrial through the trial supervision procedure. Subsequently, Jinli Company, as the agent of Aojinli Company, together with Aojinli Company as co-plaintiffs, filed this lawsuit before the Liaoning Provincial High People's Court. The subject matter of the parties, the claims, and the reasons are identical to the relevant facts in the case dismissed by Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310. Accordingly, the first-instance court should have either refused to accept the case or dismissed the lawsuit under Article 111, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China." Second, Jinli Company is not a proper party in this case. From the filing of the complaint to the conclusion of the first-instance trial, Jinli Company consistently claimed to be the agent of Aojinli Company and never asserted rights in its own name. (2) Jinli Company's claim has exceeded the statute of limitations. From 1993 until the conclusion of the first-instance trial, Jinli Company never asserted rights against Far East Company in its own name. The three repayment letters issued by Far East Company to Aojinli Company were false materials provided at the request of the other party, intended for Aojinli Company to use for accounting inspections and to respond to Jinshu Company's demands for payment. Bai Baoshan issued a "Explanation of Fund Occupation" to Far East Company, clearly stating that the repayment letters could not be used as the legal basis for finalizing the issue. In 2002, the "Notice of Demand for Payment of Arrears" served by Aojinli Company and Jinli Company to Far East Company clearly indicated that the creditor was Aojinli Company, not Jinli Company, and that the notice could serve as a transfer of rights, indicating that Jinli Company had waived its own rights. (3) The first-instance judgment erroneously held the "Joint Development Agreement" invalid. The first-instance court held that the land under the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" obtained by Far East Company on July 19, 1999, was not the plot agreed to be transferred by Far East Company and Jinli Company, and accordingly concluded that Far East Company did not obtain the land use certificate for the agreed plot. This is inconsistent with the facts. In reality, the land under the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" obtained by Far East Company on July 19, 1999, is the land agreed upon by the parties. When Far East Company signed the "Development Contract" with the Yacht Club, the Dalian Municipal Government of Liaoning Province was re-planning the Jinshitan area, and the precise location of the plot obtained by Far East Company could not be determined at that time. Therefore, the parties specially agreed that the specific location would be subject to the final planning map. In the "Joint Development Agreement" signed by Far East Company and Jinli Company, only "the land of the member villa area of the Jinshitan China International Yacht Club" was stipulated, and the specific location was to be determined after the Dalian Municipal Government issued the planning map. At the same time, Far East Company provided Jinli Company with a copy of the "Development Contract" signed with the Yacht Club to enable an accurate understanding of the specific circumstances of the transferred plot. On March 10, 1995, Far East Company sent a letter to Jinli Company, informing it that due to government planning adjustments, the location of the originally agreed plot had shifted slightly. Jinli Company did not raise any objection. On November 18, 1995, Bai Baoshan, in the "Explanation of Fund Occupation," explicitly stated: "For items not performed under the previous contract, performance will continue in the future," which sufficiently indicates that Jinli Company accepted the adjustment of the plot location. Far East Company obtained the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" for the adjusted plot accepted by the other party before the first-instance lawsuit was filed. According to Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers to Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Real Estate Development and Operation Before the Implementation of the Law on the Administration of Real Estate," the "Joint Development Agreement" signed by Far East Company and Jinli Company should be deemed valid.

Jinli Company and Aojinli Company defended, arguing that the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. They requested that the court of second instance dismiss Far East Company's appeal in accordance with the law. The main reasons are as follows: (1) The first-instance court's acceptance of Jinli Company's lawsuit complies with Article 142 of the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," which states: "Where a lawsuit is dismissed by a ruling of non-acceptance or dismissal, if the plaintiff sues again and meets the conditions for filing a lawsuit, the people's court shall accept it." Jinli Company and Aojinli Company were co-plaintiffs in the first instance, and both have the right to sue in this case. The Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310 of the Liaoning Provincial High People's Court does not involve Jinli Company, and that ruling did not dispose of Aojinli Company's substantive rights. The claims in this case are different from those in the case dismissed by Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310. In the previous lawsuit, the interest claimed for the principal of RMB 13.5 million was RMB 6 million, while in this case, Jinli Company claims interest of RMB 17 million on the principal of RMB 13.5 million. Therefore, the first-instance court's acceptance of this case complies with the law and does not constitute res judicata. (2) As a party to the contract, Jinli Company is entitled to the right to sue under the law. The court of first instance has found that the parties signing the "Joint Development Agreement" were Far East Company and Jinli Company, not as Far East Company claims that it required an application to enjoy the right to sue. (3) The statute of limitations has not expired in this case. In cases of land use right transfer contracts, as long as the transferring party has not received the transfer fee, or the receiving party has not obtained the land, the statute of limitations may be interrupted. Jinli Company and Aojinli Company have never waived their right to demand repayment of principal and interest from Far East Company. (4) The first-instance judgment's determination of the validity of the "Joint Development Agreement" is correct. The land under the "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" obtained by Far East Company in July 1999 is not the land agreed upon by Far East Company and Jinli Company, and Far East Company has not obtained legal procedures for the land agreed upon by the parties. The first-instance judgment's determination that the contract signed by the parties is invalid is correct.

The facts found by this Court are essentially consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of this Court: To resolve the dispute in this case, it must first be correctly determined whether Jinli Company or Aojinli Company has the right under the law to claim repayment of the RMB 13.5 million principal and interest from Far East Company.

(1) Regarding whether Jinli Company's filing of this lawsuit should be supported.

Although the "Joint Development Agreement" was signed by Jinli Company and Far East Company, the subsequent civil acts surrounding the joint development, such as correspondence and payments, were primarily carried out between Aojinli Company in its own name and Far East Company.

Viewing the actual performance of the "Joint Development Agreement" by the parties, the location of the plot stipulated in the agreement was adjusted due to changes in the government's planning. After Far East Company informed the other party of this, the other party did not raise any objection, indicating that Jinli Company and Aojinli Company knew of and accepted the change in the plot provided by Far East Company. Jinli Company and Aojinli Company repeatedly demanded repayment of principal and interest and specifically arranged for notarization of this matter. Far East Company repeatedly made written commitments to repay the demands of the other party, demonstrating that all parties had no intention to continue performing the "Joint Development Agreement" and had reached a consensus that Far East Company would repay the RMB 13.5 million principal and interest to Aojinli Company. Therefore, Far East Company's contractual obligation had changed from delivering the land to the other party to repaying the principal and interest to the other party.

Based on the established facts of the case, in 2002, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company served the "Notice of Demand for Payment of Arrears" to Far East Company, which clearly stated that the only creditor was Aojinli Company and that this notice could serve as a transfer of rights. This indicates that Jinli Company had transferred its right to demand repayment of principal and interest from Far East Company under the "Joint Development Agreement" to Aojinli Company. According to Articles 79 and 80 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," a creditor may transfer all or part of its contractual rights to a third party, and the transfer only requires notification to the debtor without needing the debtor's consent. Based on the actual performance of the "Joint Development Agreement" by both parties as described above, Jinli Company was legally entitled to demand repayment of principal and interest from Far East Company without needing to perform any other obligations. Therefore, it had the right to transfer this right provided that the legitimate rights and interests of Far East Company were not prejudiced. In this case, Jinli Company and Aojinli Company specifically had the content and service process of the "Notice of Demand for Payment of Arrears" notarized, which is sufficient to prove that the transfer was a true expression of their intent, and the content of the transfer does not violate legal provisions. Therefore, it should be recognized. After receiving the "Notice of Demand for Payment of Arrears," Far East Company raised no objection. This should be regarded as the parties reaching a consensus on the change of the rights holder under the "Joint Development Agreement." The notarial authority issued a formal "Notarial Certificate" with strong public evidentiary effect. This rights transfer has been completed, and the rights holder has changed from Jinli Company to Aojinli Company. After this, Jinli Company lost its standing as a creditor to demand repayment of principal and interest from Far East Company in its own name. On April 6, 2004, Jinli Company, in its own name, demanded from Far East Company the rights it had already transferred. Far East Company's objection on this ground is well-founded and should be supported.

In light of this, Jinli Company is not a proper party and does not have the right to sue in this dispute. Its lawsuit should be dismissed.

(2) Regarding whether Aojinli Company's filing of this lawsuit should be supported.

According to the established facts, before the court of first instance accepted this case, Aojinli Company filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on September 23, 2002, seeking a determination that the "Joint Development Agreement" signed by Far East Company and Jinli Company was invalid and requesting Far East Company to return the investment of RMB 13.5 million and corresponding interest. In that case, the Liaoning Provincial High People's Court dismissed Aojinli Company's lawsuit by Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310.

On April 6, 2004, Aojinli Company filed this lawsuit as a plaintiff, again seeking a determination that the "Joint Development Agreement" was invalid and requesting Far East Company to return the investment of RMB 13.5 million and corresponding interest. Except for an increase in the amount of interest, the claims and reasons are identical to those in the case dismissed by Civil Ruling (2003) Liao Min Yi Fang Zhong Zi No. 310. The increase in the amount of interest due to the passage of time does not constitute a circumstance under Article 142 of the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" where a case meeting the conditions for filing a lawsuit should be accepted. Therefore, Aojinli Company's repeated lawsuit on the same subject matter should be dismissed.

A party dissatisfied with a legally effective judgment cannot, in a subsequent lawsuit, assert positions contrary to the effective judgment or file a repeated lawsuit on the same subject matter, except by initiating a retrial through the trial supervision procedure to have the case retried. Therefore, if Aojinli Company believes it has the right to assert claims against Far East Company, it must pursue another legal avenue.

In summary, in accordance with Article 108, Article 111, Item (5), and Article 140, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the ruling is as follows:

1. Revoke Civil Judgment (2004) Liao Min Yi Fang Chu Zi No. 9;

2. Dismiss the lawsuit filed by Liaoning Jinli Housing Industry Company against Dalian Far East Housing Development Company on April 6, 2004;

3. Dismiss the lawsuit filed by Liaoning Aojinli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. against Dalian Far East Housing Development Company on April 6, 2004.

一审案件受理费50元、二审案件受理费50元共计100元，由辽宁金利房屋实业公司和辽宁澳金利房地产开发有限公司各负担50元。

本裁定为终审裁定。
